title: BIO 102 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER SIX( INTRODUCTORY MOLECULAR BIOLOGY )
subject: BIO 102

questions.question: Nucleic acids occur in every living cell where they function as which type of macromolecules?
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids function as information macromolecules responsible for storage, preservation and transmission of genetic information.

questions.question: The building blocks of nucleic acids are known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids are polymers made up of simple units (monomers) known as nucleotides.

questions.question: How many main components make up a nucleotide?
questions.explanation: Nucleotides are essentially made up of three components: nitrogenous bases, pentose sugar and phosphate.

questions.question: Which pentose sugar is found in ribonucleic acid?
questions.explanation: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) contains ribose sugar.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of a nucleotide?
questions.explanation: Nucleotides are made up of nitrogenous bases, pentose sugar and phosphate, not protein.

questions.question: Which of the following are classified as purines?
questions.explanation: The purines are adenine and guanine.

questions.question: Which of the following are classified as pyrimidines?
questions.explanation: The pyrimidines are cytosine, thymine and uracil.

questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is found in DNA but replaced by uracil in RNA?
questions.explanation: Thymine of DNA is replaced by Uracil in RNA.

questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains uracil, whereas DNA contains thymine.

questions.question: When a nitrogenous base binds to a pentose sugar, the product is known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: When a nitrogenous base binds to a pentose sugar, the product is known as a nucleoside.

questions.question: Which type of bond links a nitrogenous base to a pentose sugar?
questions.explanation: The nitrogenous base binds to a pentose sugar through an N-β-glycosidic bond.

questions.question: A purine base binds with which nitrogen to the pentose sugar?
questions.explanation: The purine binds with its 9th nitrogen to the 1st carbon of the ribose.

questions.question: A pyrimidine base binds with which nitrogen to the pentose sugar?
questions.explanation: The pyrimidine binds with its 1st nitrogen to the 1st carbon of the ribose.

questions.question: When a nucleoside enters into an ester linkage with a phosphate group, the product is known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: When a nucleoside enters into an ester linkage with a phosphate group, the product is a nucleotide.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a nucleotide?
questions.explanation: Adenosine 5'-monophosphate is an example of a nucleotide.

questions.question: DNA is characterized by which type of configuration?
questions.explanation: DNA engages in base pairing leading to its double stranded nature and an alpha-helical configuration.

questions.question: The double strands of DNA have the attribute of being complementary and what else?
questions.explanation: The double strands of DNA have the additional attribute of being complementary and also anti-parallel.

questions.question: If one strand of DNA runs in the 5' to 3' direction, the complementary strand runs in which direction?
questions.explanation: If one strand runs in the 5' to 3' direction, the complementary strand runs in the 3' to 5' direction.

questions.question: In eukaryotic cells, which proteins bind to chromosomal DNA to form nucleoproteins?
questions.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, lysine- and arginine-rich proteins called histones bind to chromosomal DNA to form nucleoproteins.

questions.question: Histones are rich in which amino acids?
questions.explanation: Histones are lysine- and arginine-rich proteins.

questions.question: Where are nucleoproteins housed within the cell?
questions.explanation: Nucleoproteins are housed within the nucleus.

questions.question: The relationship between DNA, RNA and Proteins is generally described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: This relationship is generally described as the central dogma of molecular biology.

questions.question: Originally, it was believed that information flow was in which direction?
questions.explanation: Originally it was believed that information flow was in one direction.

questions.question: Which entity came into the purview of molecular biology and showed that information can also flow from RNA to DNA?
questions.explanation: When retrovirus came into the purview of molecular biology it became clear that information can also flow from RNA to DNA.

questions.question: Replication involves the DNA-directed synthesis of which molecule?
questions.explanation: Replication involves the DNA-directed synthesis of DNA.

questions.question: Which enzyme causes the unwinding of the gene during replication?
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase causes the unwinding of the gene during replication.

questions.question: Replication gives rise to two new strands, resulting in what type of copy?
questions.explanation: Replication gives rise to a faithful copy of self.

questions.question: Replication is sometimes described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Replication is also sometimes described as duplication.

questions.question: Transcription is the DNA-directed synthesis of which molecule?
questions.explanation: Transcription is the DNA-directed synthesis of RNA.

questions.question: In transcription, which enzyme is directed to unwind the gene?
questions.explanation: In transcription, the DNA directs the RNA polymerase to unwind the gene.

questions.question: During transcription, the thymine of DNA is replaced by which base in RNA?
questions.explanation: In the course of transcription, the thymine of DNA is replaced by uracil of RNA.

questions.question: The primary transcript remains in the nucleus until it has undergone what?
questions.explanation: The primary transcript remains in the nucleus until it has undergone some post-transcriptional changes referred to as processing.

questions.question: Processing of the primary transcript results in the generation of which molecule?
questions.explanation: Processing results in the generation of a mature messenger RNA.

questions.question: The mature mRNA leaves the nucleus for which cytoplasmic structures?
questions.explanation: The mature mRNA leaves the nucleus for the ribosomes in the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Translation is the actual synthesis of which molecule on the ribosome?
questions.explanation: Translation is the actual synthesis of polypeptide on the ribosome.

questions.question: During translation, the information contained in mRNA serves as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The information contained in the mRNA serves as a template for the assembly of amino acids.

questions.question: The 4-letter language of nucleic acid guides the 20-letter language of which sequence?
questions.explanation: The 4-letter language of nucleic acid guides the 20-letter language of amino acid sequence.

questions.question: Which RNA ferries activated amino acids to the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA (tRNA) ferries activated amino acids to the site.

questions.question: Which molecule guides the linear sequence of assemblage and determines initiation and termination?
questions.explanation: The genetic code guides the linear sequence of assemblage in addition to determining the points of initiation and termination.

questions.question: What needs a signal to initiate transcription?
questions.explanation: The tightly packaged and protected chromatin needs a signal to initiate transcription.

questions.question: DNA is unpacked by processes which include DNA demethylation and what else?
questions.explanation: DNA is unpacked by processes which include DNA demethylation and histone acetylation.

questions.question: The primary transcript is a heteronuclear RNA containing expressible exons and what else?
questions.explanation: The primary transcript contains expressible exons and the intervening non-coding sequences called introns.

questions.question: Processing involves excision of introns and the ligase binding of which sequences?
questions.explanation: Processing involves excision of introns and the ligase binding of exons.

questions.question: Capping and polyadenylation of the tail produce which molecule?
questions.explanation: Capping and polyadenylation of the tail produce a mature mRNA.

questions.question: Post-translational modification of the polypeptide generates which molecule?
questions.explanation: Post-translational modification generates an active protein.

questions.question: What guides the active protein to its cellular destination?
questions.explanation: The active protein is chaperoned to its cellular destination.

questions.question: The active protein has a dynamic cycle which involves degradation at a precise point in time called what?
questions.explanation: Degradation occurs at a precise point in time (its half-life).

questions.question: Which bond is formed between the phosphate group and the sugar in a nucleotide?
questions.explanation: The ester bond is formed via the 5' carbon of the ribose.

questions.question: What is the monomer that serves as the building block for nucleic acids?
questions.explanation: The monomer nucleotides form the building blocks for the nucleic acids.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for the anti-parallel nature of DNA?
questions.explanation: The way the nitrogenous bases are arranged on the sugar phosphate backbone enables the DNA to engage in base pairing leading to its double stranded nature and an alpha-helical configuration.
